extracted.intended_audience: photojournalists, documentary photographers, multimedia journalists, editors, and contest coordinators submitting to the POY competition
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and entry standards for submitting work to the 76th Pictures of the Year International competition, covering acceptable subject/theme, technical and editorial standards (context and post-production), rights, eligibility, and prize categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission: recognize excellence in documentary photography and photojournalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Pictures of the Year International is to recognize excellence in documentary photography and photojournalism, within still photography, motion photojournalism (videography) and visual editing in both print and online formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants should submit work that demonstrates excellence in documentary storytelling and standards appropriate to stills, motion, and visual editing across print and online media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guiding principle: 'Show truth with a camera' (Spirit of the Competition)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Show truth with a camera," remains the guiding principle as articulated by POY founder Cliff Edom in 1943.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All entrants (photographers, editors, contest coordinators) are required to accept the Spirit of the Competition standards when entering. Submissions should adhere to truthful documentary/photojournalistic practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for context of images and digital post-production corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Pictures of the Year International sets the following criteria for the context of images as well as digital post-production image corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page asserts specific standards govern image context and permissible digital post-production corrections; entrants must accept and follow those standards. (The specific allowable corrections and contextual rules are referenced but not detailed in this excerpt.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Theme: Documentary Photojournalism
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should fit the competition's stated theme of documentary photojournalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page includes an eligibility section header; entrants must meet the competition's eligibility rules (details not provided in this excerpt).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyrights & Usage Rights (submission condition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pictures of the Year International (POY) recognizes and respects that copyrights are held by the photographer and/or news organization. I grant permission to Pictures of the Year International and the Missouri School of Journalism to use my submitted photographs in exhibitions, in publications, and in promotions of the competition itself, and for educational, research, and historical record purposes concerning Pictures of the Year International.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This usage includes, but is not limited to, slides/tapes, television film/tapes, videodisc, DVDs, CDs, websites, and any other type of mechanical, electronic, or digital dissemination system. Winning photographs, published tearsheets, editing displays, multimedia productions, and other images selected for historic significance become part of the permanent POY Archive. Entrants retain copyright but grant these usage rights as a condition of entering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prizes and award categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Prizes: $1,000 cash prizes & Tiffany crystal trophies for top Premier winners (Photographer of the Year; Documentary Project of the Year; World Understanding Award). $500 cash prizes & Tiffany crystal trophies for top Premier winners (Newspaper Photographer of the Year; Sports Photographer of the Year; Multimedia Photographer of the Year; Environmental Vision Award; Community Awareness Award; Best Photography Book Award). Individual category winner: 1st — Engraved plaque awards; 2nd, 3rd, & AE — Certificate awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The competition organizes awards by named categories and assigns specific cash/prize levels and trophies/plaques/certificates; entrants should identify the appropriate category for their work and be aware of prize expectations.
